facts.title: Westminster's time is coming to an end, Welsh, Scottish, Northern Irish leaders say
facts.summary: The leaders of Plaid Cymru, SNP and Sinn Fein say the UK government should prepare for constitutional change.
facts.article_excerpt: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, John Swinney, Rhun ap Iorwerth, Mary Lou McDonald and Michelle O'Neill met in Cardiff Bay on Monday The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have declared that Westminster's time is coming to an end , and that the UK government should prepare for constitutional change. The nationalist leaders from Plaid Cymru, Sinn Féin and the SNP - who want their countries to leave the United Kingdom - signed an agreement on Monday which said no Westminster government had the right to block democracy . But while Scotland's John Swinney and Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill called for referendums at a joint press conference, Wales' Rhun ap Iorwerth refused to give a timetable for one in his country. Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald also attended. Ap Iorwerth will hold further talks with Swinney in the afternoon in their roles as government leaders, with both men expected to sign an agreement on future collaboration in areas of shared interest . For the first time since devolution began, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland all have first ministers who want to leave the United Kingdom. All three met on Monday as representatives of their parties. The memorandum of understanding said: For people watching across these islands - for people watching around the world - there could be no clearer sign that Westminster's time is coming to an end. No Westminster government has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future. We recognise that our parties have different constitutional positions and that each nation will determine its own future in its own way and in its own time. draft.headline: Three UK nations' leaders say Westminster's time is ending
draft.caption:
The leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland signed an agreement saying the United Kingdom's current setup is running out of time 🇬🇧

They met in Cardiff Bay on Monday. All three lead parties that want their nations out of the UK: Plaid Cymru in Wales, the SNP in Scotland, and Sinn Fein in Northern Ireland. Their agreement says the UK government should start preparing for constitutional change.

"No Westminster government has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future."

This has never happened before. Since devolution began, meaning each nation got its own government, this is the first time all three have first ministers who want to leave.

The catch is that they are not moving at the same speed. Scotland's John Swinney and Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill called for referendums at a joint press conference. Wales' Rhun ap Iorwerth would not give a timetable. The agreement itself says each nation decides in its own way and in its own time, which is another way of saying no date exists yet.

If you had to guess, is this the start of a real breakup or a statement with no calendar behind it? 🤔

Source: BBC

threads_chain: 英國三個地方的首席部長週一一起簽了字，說西敏寺的時代要結束了。最意外的是，這是權力下放以來第一次，威爾斯、蘇格蘭、北愛爾蘭同時由主張脫離英國的人當家。

他們簽的備忘錄寫得很直白：沒有任何一個西敏寺政府有權阻擋民主，也無權動搖人民自己決定未來這個原則。

三個人分別是威爾斯的 Rhun ap Iorwerth、蘇格蘭的 John Swinney、北愛爾蘭的 Michelle O'Neill，背後是 Plaid Cymru、SNP 和 Sinn Féin。Sinn Féin 黨主席 Mary Lou McDonald 也到場。

不過三邊的腳步差很多。Swinney 跟 O'Neill 在聯合記者會上直接喊公投，ap Iorwerth 連時間表都不肯給。備忘錄自己也留了後路，寫說各自的國家會用各自的方式、在各自的時間決定未來，等於沒有人訂日期。

ap Iorwerth 只說，五月的威爾斯選舉是一個轉捩點。
